nodes.label: OSC Internal Knowledge Assistant
nodes.rationale: A provider-agnostic RAG question-answering service over OSC's internal documents. Retrieves passages, generates a grounded answer, attaches citations, and abstains rather than guessing when the corpus does not support an answer. Status: Phase 2, verified end to end on a local stack, not production-ready.

nodes.label: Vendor Agnosticism (the distinguishing constraint)
nodes.rationale: Chat model, embedding model, reranker, vector store and chunker are each selected by configuration and swappable independently, because the team expects to swap LLMs/embedders/rerankers frequently and that must be cheap. Enforced by one rule: business logic imports `protocols` and `types` only and never imports a provider module — checkable with a grep. 13 chat providers, 11 embedding providers, 3 rerankers, 3 vector stores, 2 chunkers registered; adding another is a new file plus one import line.

nodes.label: The Five Protocol Seams
nodes.rationale: Structural typing (Protocol), not base classes: a provider is compatible by virtue of its shape. No inheritance, nothing to register beyond the factory, and a test double becomes indistinguishable from a real provider — which is what makes the API tests meaningful. Total surface is about 120 lines, which is also the evidence used to reject LangChain/LlamaIndex.

nodes.label: ChatModel Protocol
nodes.rationale: complete() / stream(); declares supports_citations so the citation capability flag lives in the adapter and no business logic branches on provider identity.

nodes.label: EmbeddingModel Protocol
nodes.rationale: embed_documents() / embed_query(); declares dimensions. The declared width is injected into the vector store by the container because the store cannot know it itself.

nodes.label: VectorStore Protocol
nodes.rationale: replace_document(), delete_document(), three search methods, hash listing. This protocol is explicitly named as the swap point where a dedicated vector database would be introduced if vector search p95 degrades or the corpus exceeds a few million chunks.

nodes.label: Reranker Protocol
nodes.rationale: rerank(query, candidates, top_k). Defaults to noop because there is no golden set to demonstrate the cross-encoder improves anything.

nodes.label: Chunker Protocol
nodes.rationale: split(document) -> list[Chunk].

nodes.label: Shared Domain Vocabulary (types.py)
nodes.rationale: Document, Chunk, EmbeddedChunk, ScoredChunk, ChatRequest, Citation, Answer — all frozen dataclasses, the only vocabulary shared across modules. Deliberately the largest shared surface so that business logic needs nothing else besides protocols. RetrievalResult is flagged as the only unfrozen dataclass, a known inconsistency.

nodes.label: Registry and Composition Root
nodes.rationale: Five Registry instances map a provider name to a factory; a provider module registers itself on import and container.py imports the providers package once, so nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation. Container builds components lazily via cached_property, so `osc-assistant ingest` never constructs a chat model and therefore never needs an LLM credential.

nodes.label: ComponentConfig as Architectural Hub
nodes.rationale: Betweenness centrality in the generated knowledge graph identifies ComponentConfig (bridging 15 communities) and Document (bridging 15) as the true architectural hubs — configuration and the corpus record are what the whole system routes through, which matches the intended design.

nodes.label: StubEmbeddingModel Is the Most Connected Node
nodes.rationale: A test double has 57 edges, more than VectorStore, Document or any real provider. The graph is reporting that the test suite, not production wiring, is what actually exercises every seam — expected when all providers are optional extras, but it means the seams are proven against stubs far more than against real providers.
nodes.norm_label: stubembeddingmodel is the most connected node

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval by Default
nodes.rationale: Internal corpora are dense with acronyms, product codenames and error strings that semantic search handles badly, and paraphrase that keyword search handles badly. Postgres provides both indexes, so the marginal cost is one query and a fusion step. Explicitly framed as avoiding a known failure mode, not premature optimisation.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (dual implementation)
nodes.rationale: The same RRF formula is implemented twice — in fusion.py for the memory store and in SQL inside the pgvector store — deliberately, so both stores rank identically and swapping the vector store cannot change result ordering.

nodes.label: Abstention Is Architectural, Not a Prompt
nodes.rationale: No retrieval hits means the model is never called, because generating from nothing is guessing. No citations means the answer is treated as ungrounded. In streaming mode the final `complete` event is authoritative and the client discards what it already rendered — a policy that only held when not streaming would be worse than none.
nodes.norm_label: abstention is architectural, not a prompt

nodes.label: Grounded Generation with Citations
nodes.rationale: The answerer builds a ChatRequest with a frozen system prompt and the retrieved chunks as sources; both citation paths converge on one Citation shape so nothing downstream branches on provider.

nodes.label: Native Citations Where Available, Markers Elsewhere
nodes.rationale: Anthropic passes sources as structured documents and returns per-span citations verified against the source text; every other provider renders sources into the prompt and parses [n] markers back out. Both produce the same Citation object, so nothing downstream — including the UI — can tell the difference. A deliberate trade-off for vendor agnosticism: the first verifies a citation, the second only asserts one. The gap is supposed to be quantified by the evaluation harness that does not yet exist.
nodes.norm_label: native citations where available, markers elsewhere

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Containment via Per-Request Nonce
nodes.rationale: Titles were escaped but bodies were not, so a document containing </source></sources> closed the data block and landed its own text where the model reads it as instruction — reproduced. Fixed with a per-request nonce in the delimiter. Escaping bodies was explicitly rejected because it would corrupt the technical content this corpus is full of, turning <div> into <div> for the model to quote back. Mitigated, not eliminated: a document can still argue with the system prompt, only not impersonate it.
nodes.norm_label: prompt injection containment via per-request nonce

nodes.label: Metadata Double-Encoding Defect (pgvector)
nodes.rationale: The connection registers a jsonb codec whose encoder is json.dumps, and replace_document also called json.dumps, so Postgres stored JSON inside a JSON string and every read produced str where the domain type promises a Mapping. Nothing crashed because nothing checks at runtime, so any future metadata filtering would have failed inexplicably. Found the first time the previously unverified PostgreSQL layer was actually run — exactly the class of bug the untested-storage warning existed to flag.

nodes.label: Prune Data-Loss Guard (unreadable-file exemption)
nodes.rationale: _prune deletes anything indexed but absent from the current sync. A file that failed to parse is absent from the sync yet present at the source, so a corrupt byte — or simply deploying without the `documents` extra installed — would have deleted every PDF from the index, reporting deleted=N as if routine. Loaders now record LoadFailure and the pipeline exempts those ids from pruning, treating them as present-but-unreadable.

nodes.label: Ingestion Data-Loss Defect and replace_document
nodes.rationale: The pipeline wrote the content hash before the chunks in three un-transacted calls; a crash in between left a current hash with zero chunks, so every later sync skipped the document as already-indexed — silently invisible forever while the report counted success. A plain reorder was impossible because chunks reference the document row via a foreign key, so upsert + record_document were replaced with a single transactional replace_document(document, chunks). Notably the protocol got smaller: two methods out, one in.

nodes.label: Chunker Content-Corruption Defect
nodes.rationale: Separators were re-attached as part + separator, appending one to the final fragment that was never there — 287 characters in, 286 out, with a doubled period. In a system whose trust model is 'click the citation and verify', the indexed text was not the source text and the Anthropic path was quoting it back as verbatim evidence. Fixed with a split guaranteeing ''.join(parts) == text.

nodes.label: Parsers Extract and Never Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Chunk text is quoted back as citation evidence, so invented or normalised text would make that evidence a forgery. This is the same trust-model argument that governs the chunker's content-preservation guarantee.

nodes.label: Multi-Format Document Parsing
nodes.rationale: Extension → extraction function: Markdown/text read directly, HTML through the stdlib html.parser (dropping <script>/<style>, preferring the document's own <title>), PDF through pypdf per page retaining page_count, .docx through python-docx including table cells — because policy documents keep the facts people actually ask about inside tables.

nodes.label: Text Extraction Is a Plain Dict, Not a Registry
nodes.rationale: The five component seams use Registry[T] because they are selected by a configuration name and need per-provider options. A parser is selected by file extension and takes no options, so PARSERS: dict[str, Parser] is the whole mechanism. Reaching for the heavier abstraction would have added indirection without removing a line — a direct application of the handbook's 'avoid unnecessary abstractions' rule.
nodes.norm_label: text extraction is a plain dict, not a registry

nodes.label: Idempotent Ingestion by Content Hash
nodes.rationale: Content-hash skip, incremental re-index, pruning and per-document failure isolation. Re-running an unchanged corpus makes zero embedding calls, which is asserted by a test and was verified manually (indexed=0 skipped=7 in 0.07s). Known limitation: _prune assumes a single writer — it reads the document-hash map at the start of a sync and deletes anything absent at the end, so a concurrent writer's documents would be deleted.

nodes.label: One Datastore (PostgreSQL holds everything)
nodes.rationale: One PostgreSQL database holds chunk text, embeddings (pgvector), the lexical tsvector index and document metadata. A chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup to take, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip instead of a fan-out. A dedicated vector database earns its place only when vector search p95 degrades or the corpus passes a few million chunks.

nodes.label: pgvector Vector Store
nodes.rationale: Largest file in the codebase (379 lines). Applies migrations/001_init.sql through a hand-rolled forward-only runner, substituting the embedding dimension into the DDL at migration time. Verified for the first time against PostgreSQL 18.4 with pgvector 0.8.2: all eleven integration tests pass, covering the migration runner, generated tsvector column, SQL rank fusion, the replace_document transaction, cascade deletion and workspace isolation.

nodes.label: Conditional HNSW Index (2000-dimension limit)
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX USING hnsw is capped at 2000 dimensions by pgvector, and the previous default profile specified text-embedding-3-large at 3072 — the first real migration on the old default would have aborted outright. The index is now created only when the dimension is ≤ 2000, with a warning; above it the column is left unindexed and vector search degrades to an exact scan. Correct but O(n), so check this before choosing a wide embedding model.

nodes.label: Vector Width Is Fixed at Migration Time
nodes.rationale: Changing the embedding model changes the vector width, which is fixed in the DDL when the chunks table is created. It requires a new database (or a dropped chunks table) and a full re-index. The store asserts dimensions match at startup and refuses to run otherwise, rather than silently comparing incompatible vectors. This is why every experiment profile names its own database.
nodes.norm_label: vector width is fixed at migration time

nodes.label: workspace_id Partition Key from Day One
nodes.rationale: Explicitly acknowledged as the only speculative design in the codebase, and defended on migration cost: adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration, whereas carrying it now costs one column and one index prefix. Schema-complete and honoured by every query, but single-tenant in practice — only one workspace exists and nothing resolves a workspace from a request.
nodes.norm_label: workspace_id partition key from day one

nodes.label: No LLM Framework (LangChain/LlamaIndex rejected)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated and rejected on evidence, per the stated requirement to judge frameworks pragmatically. The seams this system needs are five protocols totalling about 120 lines; a framework would impose its own document and retriever abstractions on top of ours, add a large transitive dependency tree, and place an uncontrolled layer on the exact code path that most needs tracing and tuning. Provider SDKs are used directly, each as an optional extra.

nodes.label: One Adapter for Eight Services (openai_compatible)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, Hugging Face, OpenRouter and Together all speak /v1/chat/completions, so one adapter is registered under separate provider names with base URL and credential env var pre-filled. Eight adapters would have been eight places to fix the same bug. The single adapter serves 11 registered chat provider names.

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts (module constants, no interpolation)
nodes.rationale: Any dynamic value would break prefix caching for every request and make evaluation results unattributable to a reviewable string. The discipline is kept even though the saving is currently zero.

nodes.label: Prompt Caching — Implemented but Inert
nodes.rationale: cache_system_prompt marks the Anthropic system block cacheable, but ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT is roughly 250 tokens — below the minimum cacheable prefix on current models — so cache_read_input_tokens is zero on every request. Doubly inert now that the default stack is Ollama, which has no such feature. Kept because the discipline is correct and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Reasoning Control Is Configuration, Not Code
nodes.rationale: Qwen3's thinking is disabled with extra_body.reasoning_effort: none through the adapter's existing pass-through for vendor-specific parameters — no new code path, and it works for any reasoning model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Only the consequences of reasoning needed code (stripping a leaked <think> block before citation parsing, reporting an exhausted budget instead of silently abstaining), because those are correctness concerns rather than tuning.
nodes.norm_label: reasoning control is configuration, not code

nodes.label: 4096-Token Context Budget Constraint
nodes.rationale: Ollama loads qwen3:8b with a 4096-token window, which caps the corpus sent to the model at five chunks of ~900 characters. A document needing six passages is answered incompletely rather than incorrectly. chunk_size, top_k and max_tokens are all sized to this window; raising any of them without serving a larger context pushes the answer out of the window.

nodes.label: The Local Model Misreads Figures
nodes.rationale: Observed directly: asked for expense approval thresholds, qwen3:8b rendered the source's '500 to 2,500 EUR' as '50,000 to 2,500 EUR' while citing the correct passage. Retrieval right, citation right, number wrong. The central honest caveat of the local stack: citations tell a user where to check, and on an 8B model they genuinely have to. hosted-anthropic.yaml exists partly as the comparison point for quantifying this gap.

nodes.label: Query Rewriting (implemented, disabled by default)
nodes.rationale: Resolves conversational references into a standalone query using the configured fast model; best-effort, any failure falls back to the original question. Disabled by default because it was never justified by measurement and on the local stack it costs a second Qwen3 call on the critical path. The UI correspondingly sends no history, so follow-up turns are independent questions. Turning both on together is the right move once a golden set can show it helps.

nodes.label: min_score Applied Before Reranking
nodes.rationale: The threshold was being compared against an undefined scale: first-stage scores are on a known scale, but a cross-encoder logit is unbounded and often negative for a relevant passage, so thresholding reranker output would have emptied the result set the moment a reranker was enabled. Now applied to first-stage scores, with a regression test using a negative-scoring reranker.

nodes.label: Evaluation Harness (the highest-leverage missing piece)
nodes.rationale: Designed as a first-class subsystem: 50-100 real questions curated with OSC employees, retrieval metrics (recall@10, MRR) and generation metrics (citation coverage, faithfulness), runnable as `make eval` and gating CI. None of it exists, so every quality claim in the status document is unmeasurable and every retrieval/generation setting in default.yaml is an educated guess. It is the gate for reranking, chunk-size tuning, query rewriting and the local-vs-hosted decision.

nodes.label: OIDC Authentication (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: No identity anywhere; /api/chat and /api/search accept arbitrary unauthenticated input, and a UI at / makes the service look ready to use. Intended design is OIDC against OSC's existing IdP with group membership feeding access control. Smallest interim fix named: refuse to start when environment != development and no auth is configured — ten lines, and the constraint moves from prose into the code path.

nodes.label: Per-Document Access Control (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: Design calls for ACLs resolved at index time and enforced as a SQL predicate at query time, so an unauthorised chunk is never retrieved and never reaches the model. Phase 1 was scoped to company-wide-readable content specifically to avoid needing this yet. Known future limitation: ACLs will be a point-in-time snapshot, so a permission revoked between syncs is not reflected until the next one.

nodes.label: Fully Local Default Stack
nodes.rationale: Ollama qwen3:8b for generation, Ollama nomic-embed-text (768-d) for embeddings, PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector 0.8.2 for storage. No credential required and no corpus text leaves the host. Reference environment verified: PostgreSQL 18.4 / pgvector 0.8.2, Ollama 0.32.5 at a 4096-token context. Note qwen3:8b reports capabilities completion/tools/thinking and cannot embed, which is why a separate embedding model is required.

nodes.label: Speculative Code with No Consumer
nodes.rationale: Flagged as debt: the native Gemini providers are ~330 lines plus a google-genai dependency reaching a service the gemini_openai preset already reaches through a shipped, tested adapter; and FixedSizeChunker is an evaluation baseline for an evaluation harness that does not exist. Both violate the handbook's rule that every abstraction must solve a real engineering problem.

nodes.label: 'local' Provider Name Means Two Different Things
nodes.rationale: In llm_registry `local` is an OpenAI-compatible server on :8000; in embedding_registry it is sentence-transformers. Same token, two unrelated behaviours, coexisting in the same profile file. Proposed fix: rename the LLM one to openai_local.
nodes.norm_label: 'local' provider name means two different things

nodes.label: settings.py Has Zero Tests
nodes.rationale: It carries the only hand-written logic an operator will touch — a custom YAML settings source and four-layer precedence. Nothing verifies that env overrides YAML, that nested OSC_LLM__PROVIDER merges rather than replacing the whole block, or that a missing profile is tolerated. A precedence regression is invisible in tests and surfaces as 'production is running the wrong model'.

nodes.label: Provider Resources Are Never Released
nodes.rationale: Container.shutdown() closes only the vector store. VoyageEmbeddingModel opens an httpx.AsyncClient and defines an aclose() nothing calls; OpenAI and Gemini clients are never closed. Harmless at process exit, a leak in tests and any future in-process reload.

nodes.label: Integration Suite Shares the Application Database
nodes.rationale: Isolation is by workspace_id and is honoured, but a test run against a production DSN would write to production. Also forces OSC_TEST_DIMENSIONS to match the width the chunks table was migrated with (768). Smallest fix: a dedicated test database, and refuse to run when the DSN matches the configured application DSN.
nodes.norm_label: integration suite shares the application database

nodes.label: Test Suite (119 tests, 0 skipped)
nodes.rationale: Runs the real pipelines — real container, real retrieval, real answerer — against in-process implementations of the protocols, registered through the ordinary registry, which is the same path a new provider takes. 108 run with no network/DB/credentials; ruff and mypy --strict clean across 45 source files. Three tests are regressions for defects actually reproduced, not speculative. Four material gaps: the end-to-end path is manual, no hosted provider has ever been called, settings.py is untested, and answer quality is unmeasured.

nodes.label: Generated Knowledge Graph and Its Caveats
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ generated 2026-07-29 from 62 files: 812 nodes, 1973 edges, 36 communities, with wiki/index.md as the agent entry point. Caveats: it predates the parsers/UI/new tests; migrations/001_init.sql is absent because tree_sitter_sql was not installable, so the tables, indexes and the foreign key that forced the replace_document design are invisible; and 135 dangling-endpoint edges, 5 self-loops and 100 collapsed undirected edges mean the edge count understates the raw extraction.
nodes.norm_label: generated knowledge graph and its caveats

nodes.label: Make the System Verifiable Before Making It Bigger
nodes.rationale: The stated ordering principle for remaining work. The binding constraint has moved from storage (now verified) to measurement, so the evaluation harness is first, then an automated end-to-end smoke test, then auth, then ACLs, then measured retrieval tuning. Deliberately late: the web client, multi-tenancy beyond the partition key, additional providers. Deliberately absent: fine-tuning, agentic tool use, a knowledge-graph layer.
nodes.norm_label: make the system verifiable before making it bigger

nodes.label: OSC Knowledge Assistant (README overview)
nodes.rationale: Operator-facing entry point: what the service is, how to run it, and the design decisions worth knowing. Switching any component is a profile edit, not a code change.

nodes.label: Quick Start
nodes.rationale: Requires PostgreSQL with pgvector and a running Ollama with qwen3:8b and nomic-embed-text pulled. Migrations run automatically on first use, so ingest is the first command. OSC_DATABASE__DSN points at a database other than the one in config/default.yaml.

nodes.label: Module Responsibility Map
nodes.rationale: protocols/types/registries/providers/ingestion/retrieval/generation/container/api, with the api layer explicitly described as thin — validate, delegate, encode. Restates the invariant: business logic depends only on protocols and types and never imports a provider, which is what makes providers swappable.

nodes.label: Ingestion Guarantees (idempotency and failure isolation)
nodes.rationale: Idempotent by content hash: re-running over an unchanged corpus makes zero embedding calls, an edited file re-indexes alone, a deleted file is pruned with its chunks. One bad file cannot break a sync — a corrupt or password-protected document is reported and skipped, the command exits non-zero, and crucially it is not pruned because a file that failed to parse is still present at the source. Scanned PDFs are rejected explicitly rather than indexed as empty; there is no OCR.

nodes.label: Supported Formats and Extraction
nodes.rationale: Markdown/text read byte-for-byte; HTML via the standard library with script/style discarded and title used; PDF via pypdf page by page with page count retained; Word via python-docx including table cells. PDF and Word need the `documents` extra. Adding a format is a function plus one dict entry in ingestion/parsers.py; nothing else changes.

nodes.label: Layered Configuration (env > .env > YAML profile)
nodes.rationale: Every value is addressable from the environment with the OSC_ prefix and a double underscore for nesting; the active YAML profile is overridable with OSC_PROFILE. This is the mechanism that makes provider swapping a configuration change rather than a code change.

nodes.label: Running an Experiment
nodes.rationale: Copy a profile, change one thing, point OSC_PROFILE at it. hosted-anthropic.yaml moves every component to a hosted vendor and is the only configuration with provider-verified citations; local-only.yaml swaps Ollama embeddings for in-process sentence-transformers and enables the cross-encoder reranker; groq-voyage.yaml shares no vendor with either. None requires a code change — this is the working proof of the vendor-agnosticism requirement.

nodes.label: Adding a Provider
nodes.rationale: Create a module that registers a factory with the relevant registry and add it to its package __init__. No existing file changes. The class only needs the shape of protocols.ChatModel — no base class to inherit, nothing to register elsewhere.

nodes.label: Working with a Reasoning Model
nodes.rationale: Qwen3 thinks before answering, spending completion tokens that never reach the user. Disabled by default because Ollama loads the model with a 4096-token context and reasoning competes with the answer for that budget. chunk_size, top_k and max_tokens are sized to the same window. If reasoning is re-enabled, raise max_tokens with it — an exhausted budget produces no answer text at all, and the adapter reports that explicitly rather than letting it become a silent 'I could not find anything'.

nodes.label: Interfaces (CLI, HTTP, UI)
nodes.rationale: CLI: serve/ingest/ask/search/providers. HTTP: GET /api/health reporting the active component set, POST /api/search as the retrieval-only debugging surface, POST /api/chat SSE by default. UI: a single static page at /, deliberately one file with no build step, consuming the same public API as any other client and expected to be replaced by a richer one.

nodes.label: Not Yet Built / Deployment Constraint
nodes.rationale: Authentication, per-document access control, rate limiting, conversation persistence, the evaluation harness and connectors beyond the filesystem are absent. Mitigating facts: the service exposes no write endpoint (ingestion is a CLI operation), and it must sit behind the corporate identity proxy until OIDC lands.

nodes.label: OSC Engineering Handbook
nodes.rationale: The standards this repository is held to. Frames contributors as building a production system that must remain understandable for years, so every technical decision should favour long-term quality over short-term convenience.

nodes.label: Engineering Optimisation Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Correctness > reliability > maintainability > readability > scalability > performance > development speed, in that order. Never sacrifice correctness for convenience; avoid premature optimisation. This ordering is what the status document cites when defending decisions like abstention-as-architecture and hybrid retrieval.

nodes.label: Avoid Unnecessary Abstractions
nodes.rationale: Explicit prohibition on duplicated logic, dead code, unnecessary abstractions, overengineering, magic numbers and hidden side effects. Prefer composition over unnecessary inheritance; prefer the simpler solution when it achieves the same goal without sacrificing extensibility. Every abstraction must solve a real engineering problem.

nodes.label: Documentation as a First-Class Deliverable
nodes.rationale: Comments should explain why something exists, architectural intent, business rules, assumptions and edge cases — not restate the code. Documentation must explain what was built, why, and how it works, assuming future developers know nothing about today's decisions. This is why PROJECT_STATUS.md and the profile YAML files carry rationale inline.

nodes.label: Session Startup Protocol
nodes.rationale: Before implementing any feature: read PROJECT_STATUS.md, then README.md, then graphify-out/wiki/, understand the current milestone, and confirm the implementation plan before modifying code. This is the mechanism that makes the knowledge graph and status document load-bearing rather than decorative.

nodes.label: Testing Increases Confidence, Not Coverage
nodes.rationale: Prefer unit tests, edge-case testing, failure-path testing and deterministic tests. Testing should increase confidence rather than simply improve coverage — which is the standard the status document measures itself against when noting that three tests are regressions for reproduced defects and that the seams are proven against stubs more than real providers.

nodes.label: Development PostgreSQL + pgvector Service
nodes.rationale: Deliberately optional: the reference development environment uses a natively installed PostgreSQL, so this file is a convenience and not a requirement. The application creates its own schema on first use, so the service only needs to exist. Has a pg_isready healthcheck and a named volume for data.

nodes.label: pgvector Image Tag Pinning Intent
nodes.rationale: The comment states the image is pinned by digest because pg16 is a moving tag and an unannounced pgvector or server upgrade underneath a populated volume is not something to discover during an incident. The actual image line is `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` — the tag, not a digest — so the stated intent and the config disagree. PROJECT_STATUS.md §8 and §14 corroborate this: the digest is explicitly listed as not pinned, deprioritised because the compose file is now a secondary path.

nodes.label: Default Profile (fully local)
nodes.rationale: Nothing in this configuration sends corpus text or questions off the host and no API credential is required. workspace_id default, environment development, JSON logging at INFO. Every value is overridable via OSC_ env vars with double-underscore nesting; running an experiment is copying the file and pointing OSC_PROFILE at the copy.

nodes.label: Answer Model: Ollama qwen3:8b
nodes.rationale: Reached through the OpenAI-compatible adapter. include_usage_in_stream is set because Ollama reports token usage only on the final stream chunk — without it the streaming path (what the API and UI use) records zero tokens for every request, making cost and context-budget analysis impossible.

nodes.label: reasoning_effort: none (Qwen3 thinking disabled)
nodes.rationale: Measured on this deployment: 138 completion tokens with thinking versus 3 without, for the same reply. Off for two reasons — (1) Ollama loads the model with a 4096-token context and thinking competes with the answer for that budget, and an exhausted budget returns empty content rather than a short answer; (2) grounded QA over retrieved passages is mostly extractive, so the latency is not repaid. Set to low or medium to re-enable, raising generation.max_tokens to match.

nodes.label: fast_llm Seam (same model as the answerer)
nodes.rationale: Used only when retrieval.rewrite_queries is enabled. Points at the same qwen3:8b because an 8B local model is already the cheap option and a second distinct model would mean a second model load.
nodes.norm_label: fast_llm seam (same model as the answerer)

nodes.label: Embeddings: Ollama nomic-embed-text (768-d)
nodes.rationale: Chosen independently of the answer model, which is the point of the separate seam. Changing it changes the vector width and therefore requires a full re-index against a fresh chunks table. nomic-embed-text is a purpose-built retrieval embedder at 768 dimensions, comfortably inside pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW index limit.

nodes.label: Reranker: noop (deferred until measurable)
nodes.rationale: Off until the evaluation harness can show the gain on OSC's own golden set. Switching to cross_encoder is now safe to measure because min_score is applied to first-stage scores, so enabling a reranker no longer risks discarding everything.

nodes.label: Chunking Sized to the 4096-Token Context (900/120)
nodes.rationale: recursive strategy, chunk_size 900, chunk_overlap 120 — roughly 225 tokens per chunk and five chunks of sources, leaving room for the system prompt and the answer inside the answer model's 4096-token context. Both should be raised if the model is served with a larger context.

nodes.label: Retrieval: hybrid, 30 candidates → top 5
nodes.rationale: strategy hybrid, candidates 30, top_k 5, rrf_k 60, min_score 0.0. These values are tuned by reasoning against the 4096-token budget rather than by measurement, and PROJECT_STATUS.md §8 explicitly labels every retrieval and generation setting here an educated guess.

nodes.label: rewrite_queries: false
nodes.rationale: It resolves follow-up references ('what about the second one?') but costs a second model call on the critical path, and its benefit has never been measured against a golden set. The comment prescribes enabling it together with an evaluation run rather than on its own.

nodes.label: generation.max_tokens 1500, require_citations true
nodes.rationale: Must cover the answer plus any thinking the model does; 1500 keeps the whole request inside a 4096-token context alongside five chunks of sources. require_citations true is the configuration half of the abstention policy.

nodes.label: Default Database and Pool Settings
nodes.rationale: DSN postgresql://mokshdutt@localhost:5432/osc with a 1-10 connection pool — a developer-specific local DSN committed as the default, which is why README documents overriding it with OSC_DATABASE__DSN. This is also the DSN the integration suite shares, per the P1 debt item.

nodes.label: hosted-anthropic Experiment Profile
nodes.rationale: The deliberate opposite of the default: every component hosted, and the only configuration in which citations are verified against the source text rather than asserted by the model. Exists as a quality ceiling to measure the local stack against — specifically to quantify qwen3:8b's numeric-fidelity gap. claude-opus-5 with effort low and cache_system_prompt, claude-haiku-4-5 as fast_llm, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, chunk 1200/150, 40 candidates → top 8, max_tokens 4096.

nodes.label: 3072-Dimension Embedding Caveat
nodes.rationale: text-embedding-3-large is 3072-dimensional, exceeding pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW limit, so the migration leaves the column unindexed and vector search falls back to an exact scan. It also needs its own database (osc_hosted3072) because vector width is fixed when the chunks table is created. This is the exact configuration that would have aborted migration before the conditional-index fix.

nodes.label: Hosted Models Lift the Prompt Budget
nodes.rationale: Hosted models are served with a large context, so the prompt budget the local 4096-token deployment is constrained to no longer applies — chunk_size rises 900→1200, overlap 120→150, candidates 30→40, top_k 5→8 and max_tokens 1500→4096. A concrete demonstration that the local tuning is a deployment constraint, not a retrieval finding.
nodes.norm_label: hosted models lift the prompt budget

nodes.label: local-only Experiment Profile
nodes.rationale: Local without Ollama embeddings: sentence-transformers in-process plus a cross-encoder reranker. The default profile is already fully local via Ollama, so this profile exists specifically to exercise the second local embedding path and the reranker. Needs pip install -e '.[local]'.

nodes.label: BGE Asymmetric Query Prefix
nodes.rationale: bge is asymmetric: queries expect the instruction prefix 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ' while documents do not. Encoding both sides identically would degrade retrieval, so the prefix is a provider option rather than something business logic knows about.

nodes.label: 384-Dimension Database Separation
nodes.rationale: bge-small-en-v1.5 is 384-dimensional against nomic-embed-text's 768. The chunks table fixes its vector width at migration time, so this profile needs its own database (osc_local384) and a full re-index; it cannot share one with the default profile.

nodes.label: cross_encoder Reranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)
nodes.rationale: The only profile that enables reranking. It is the exercise path for the reranker seam that the default profile leaves as noop, and the configuration whose unbounded negative logits motivated moving min_score to first-stage scores.

nodes.label: OSC Knowledge Assistant Web UI
nodes.rationale: Deliberately one self-contained file with no build step and no framework, imported by nothing in the backend, so the whole UI can be replaced by swapping the single file. A richer client is the expected path.

nodes.label: renderSources
nodes.rationale: Re-renders the whole source list on every citation event rather than patching one node, because a citation can arrive for any already-rendered source and full replace is cheaper to reason about than diffing.

nodes.label: Health check status banner
nodes.rationale: Surfaces llm provider/model, embedding model, vector store provider and retrieval strategy from GET /api/health so the operator can see which configuration answered a question without reading server config.

nodes.label: SSE chat stream protocol (sources/delta/citation/complete/error)
nodes.rationale: Frames are separated by a blank line and a partial frame stays buffered, so the client can decode arbitrary chunk boundaries from the reader without a framing library.

nodes.label: Complete event is authoritative
nodes.rationale: The one rule worth preserving on a rewrite: the complete event replaces whatever streamed. When it reports an abstention the client must discard already-rendered delta text and drop the source list, because the assistant declined to answer and streamed fragments would read as a partial answer.

nodes.label: Conversation history deliberately not sent
nodes.rationale: Query rewriting is disabled by default, so sending history would make a follow-up retrieve against an unresolved reference. Single-turn requests keep retrieval grounded until rewriting exists.

nodes.label: Grounded answer / abstention contract
nodes.rationale: Answers are generated only from retrieved sources with citations; if the corpus lacks the answer the assistant says so rather than guessing. The UI states this up front so users read an abstention as correct behaviour, not failure.

nodes.label: Production deployment window
nodes.rationale: Monday to Thursday 09:00-16:00 CET. Friday deploys are blocked because the on-call rotation thins over the weekend and a Friday regression is typically only discovered on Monday. Emergency fixes need on-call engineering manager approval recorded in the incident channel.

nodes.label: Pre-deployment checklist
nodes.rationale: Green CI, second-engineer migration review, written rollback plan and feature flags off in production - each item removes one class of decision from the moment of an incident.

nodes.label: Blue-green deployment strategy
nodes.rationale: The new revision runs alongside the current one and receives no traffic until its health check passes, so a failed start never reaches a user and rollback is a traffic shift rather than a redeploy.

nodes.label: Staged traffic shift and automatic abort
nodes.rationale: 10 percent for 10 minutes, then 50 percent for 10 minutes, then 100 percent, watching error rate and p95 latency. An error rate above 2 percent aborts automatically so the blast radius is bounded without a human in the loop.
nodes.norm_label: staged traffic shift and automatic abort

nodes.label: Backward-compatible database migrations
nodes.rationale: Migrations run before the new revision takes traffic, so during the shift both revisions read the same schema; a migration that cannot be made backward compatible is split across two releases.

nodes.label: Rollback procedure
nodes.rationale: Rollback is a traffic shift to the previous revision, under two minutes, and is always the first response to a regression: traffic is made safe first and diagnosis happens afterwards.

nodes.label: Forward fix for migrations (never auto-rollback)
nodes.rationale: Migrations are never rolled back automatically because reversing a migration that has already accepted writes loses data; a forward fix is written instead.

nodes.label: Post-deployment monitoring and release log
nodes.rationale: Dashboards are watched 30 minutes past full traffic and the release is recorded with commit SHA, deployer and outcome, so a later incident can be tied to a specific revision.

nodes.label: Incident severity levels
nodes.rationale: Severity is defined by customer impact and workaround availability rather than by component, so response time can be set without debating ownership.

nodes.label: SEV1
nodes.rationale: Complete loss of a customer-facing service, confirmed data loss or a confirmed security breach. 15 minute response 24/7, incident commander appointed, executive notification mandatory.

nodes.label: SEV2
nodes.rationale: Major functionality degraded for many customers with no workaround. 30 minute response in business hours, 1 hour outside.

nodes.label: SEV3
nodes.rationale: Minor degradation or a workaround exists; response by the next business day.

nodes.label: SEV4
nodes.rationale: Cosmetic or single-customer report with no service impact; handled in the normal backlog.

nodes.label: Incident Commander
nodes.rationale: Single decision maker who coordinates and does not debug; for SEV1 the IC must not also be the primary responder, because a debugging IC stops coordinating exactly when coordination matters most.

nodes.label: Communications Lead
nodes.rationale: Owns all internal and customer updates; required for SEV1 and SEV2 so responders are not interrupted to write status posts.

nodes.label: Scribe
nodes.rationale: Keeps a timestamped log of actions and decisions, required for SEV1 - the record the postmortem is later reconstructed from.

nodes.label: Incident communication cadence
nodes.rationale: SEV1 every 30 minutes to the incident channel and the customer status page, SEV2 every 2 hours in business hours, SEV3/SEV4 on resolution only.

nodes.label: Blameless postmortem
nodes.rationale: Mandatory for SEV1 and SEV2 within 5 business days. Postmortems describe what the system did and what conditions allowed it, not who made a mistake, so responders report accurately; every action item has a named owner, a due date and backlog tracking. SEV1 postmortems are reviewed in weekly engineering leadership.

nodes.label: 60-day expense submission window
nodes.rationale: Claims go through the Expense Portal within 60 days of the cost; later claims need written justification plus finance director approval and may be declined, keeping the accounting period closable.

nodes.label: Itemised receipt requirement
nodes.rationale: Card statements are not evidence because they do not itemise. Expenses under 25 EUR are exempt, capped at 100 EUR per employee per month, so the exemption cannot become a routine channel.

nodes.label: Expense approval thresholds
nodes.rationale: Up to 500 EUR direct manager, 500-2,500 EUR department head, above 2,500 EUR finance director. Items above 2,500 EUR must be approved before the cost is incurred; retrospective approval is never granted, so the approver still has a real choice.

nodes.label: Flight class rules
nodes.rationale: Economy under six hours, premium economy at six hours or longer, business class only with finance director approval regardless of duration.

nodes.label: Accommodation caps
nodes.rationale: 180 EUR per night in tier-one cities (London, Zurich, New York, Singapore, Tokyo) and 120 EUR elsewhere; local tourist taxes sit outside the cap and are reimbursed in full because they are not discretionary.

nodes.label: Rail preferred under five hours door-to-door
nodes.norm_label: rail preferred under five hours door-to-door

nodes.label: Daily meal allowance
nodes.rationale: 65 EUR tier-one, 45 EUR elsewhere. Explicitly a cap on reimbursable spend rather than a per diem payment - only actual documented spend is reimbursed.

nodes.label: Client entertainment rules
nodes.rationale: Needs prior department head approval and a record of the names and employers of all attendees, which is what makes the spend auditable against anti-bribery expectations.

nodes.label: Non-reimbursable expenses
nodes.rationale: Never reimbursed: traffic and parking fines, duty-free purchases, personal travel insurance, hotel minibar and loyalty-programme fees.

nodes.label: Annual leave accrual and carryover
nodes.rationale: 26 days per calendar year on top of public holidays, credited monthly at 2.166 days from the first day of employment. Up to 10 unused days carry over and expire on 31 March without payout, which bounds the accrued liability on the balance sheet.

nodes.label: Leave request approval workflow
nodes.rationale: Five consecutive days or fewer needs only the direct manager; longer requests additionally need the department head and 21 days notice, so team coverage can be arranged.

nodes.label: Sick leave
nodes.rationale: 12 fully paid days per calendar year, non-accruing and non-carrying. A medical certificate is required beyond three consecutive working days; shorter absences need only a notification before 10:00 on day one. Sickness during approved annual leave can be reclassified with a certificate so holiday is not lost to illness.

nodes.label: Parental leave
nodes.rationale: 18 paid weeks for primary caregivers, 6 for secondary, taken within 12 months of birth or placement, in up to three blocks with manager agreement and 8 weeks notice.

nodes.label: Unpaid leave
nodes.rationale: Up to three months at department head discretion, only once accrued annual leave is exhausted. Benefits continue but pension contributions are suspended.

nodes.label: Public holidays
nodes.rationale: Holidays follow the employee's country of residence; for cross-region workers the contracting entity's calendar applies, giving one unambiguous calendar per employee.

nodes.label: Sabbatical
nodes.rationale: Four weeks paid, requestable after five years of continuous service.

nodes.label: Principle of least privilege
nodes.rationale: Every account gets the minimum access its role needs, and access is granted to groups rather than individual accounts so entitlements can be reasoned about and revoked as a unit.

nodes.label: Periodic access reviews
nodes.rationale: Confidential-or-higher systems quarterly, Internal annually. Reviews are run by the system owner rather than the security team because only the owner knows whether an entitlement is still justified; anything the reviewer cannot justify is revoked by default, and reviews must complete within 15 working days.

nodes.label: Joiners, movers and leavers
nodes.rationale: Joiner access is provisioned no earlier than the start date; role changes revoke prior entitlements within 5 working days because additive-only role changes are the most common source of excessive privilege at OSC; all access is revoked within 4 hours of a confirmed departure and immediately for an involuntary one.

nodes.label: Privileged production access
nodes.rationale: Hardware MFA plus just-in-time grants of at most 8 hours; standing production administrative access is not permitted for any role, so a compromised account is rarely privileged at the moment of compromise.

nodes.label: Service account controls
nodes.rationale: Every service account has a named human owner and credentials rotate every 90 days. Interactive use is forbidden and alerted on, because interactive use of a service account is the signature of credential theft.

nodes.label: OSC Data Retention Schedule
nodes.rationale: Owned by Legal and Compliance; applies to all systems processing OSC or customer data. Defines how long each data category is held and what happens at end of life.

nodes.label: Retention balance rationale
nodes.rationale: Retaining data longer than necessary increases breach impact and regulatory exposure, while deleting it too early destroys records OSC is legally required to hold. Every period in the schedule is a point between those two failures.

nodes.label: Customer account records (7 years)
nodes.rationale: Held 7 years after account closure. The period comes from financial record-keeping obligations and cannot be shortened by a deletion request.

nodes.label: Application logs (90 days hot, 12 months total)
nodes.rationale: 90 days hot storage plus 275 days cold, totalling 12 months - recent debugging stays fast while the long tail stays cheap.
nodes.norm_label: application logs (90 days hot, 12 months total)

nodes.label: Security audit logs (24 months, append-only)
nodes.rationale: Written to append-only storage and not modifiable or deletable before 24 months expire, so the audit trail survives an attacker who reaches the systems it records.

nodes.label: Email and instant messaging records (3 years)
nodes.norm_label: email and instant messaging records (3 years)

nodes.label: Recruitment records (12 or 24 months)
nodes.rationale: Unsuccessful candidate records are deleted after 12 months unless the candidate consented to a 24 month talent-pool retention - the longer period requires explicit consent rather than being the default.

nodes.label: Backup snapshots (35 days)
nodes.rationale: A deletion request is satisfied once the record leaves live systems; backups are never edited to remove individual records and instead age out naturally within 35 days, because surgically rewriting backups would destroy their restorability.

nodes.label: End-of-life deletion process
nodes.rationale: Deletion is permanent and irreversible; records are destroyed rather than anonymised unless the Data Protection Officer has approved a specific analytical need. Jobs run on the first Sunday of each month and a failed deletion raises a SEV3 incident that must be resolved before the next monthly run.

nodes.label: Legal hold
nodes.rationale: A legal hold suspends all deletion for covered records, including scheduled end-of-life deletion, and is applied and released only by the General Counsel. Held records are retained until release however long that takes, so the schedule can never destroy evidence.
